scope: Theorem 6.2 of the manuscript “Finite algebraic envelopes and the Boone–Higman conjecture” (preprints/Finite-algebraic-envelopes-and-the-Boone-Higman-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 250 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ff461d9e2465f187), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let b G be a finitely generated group with decidable word problem. There exist a finitely presented monoid K with zero Ω ̸= 1K, and a finitely generated monoid H with decidable word problem and zero ζ ̸= 1H, with the following properties. (i) There is an injective group homomorphism b G −→ H×. (ii) For the monoid T defined above, there is an injective unital monoid homomorphism κ : T −→ H with κ(0T ) = ζ. (iii) For every finite ordered tuple h1, . . . , hd of distinct nonzero elements of H, with d ≥ 1, there are L, R ∈ H such that Lh1R = 1H, LhiR = ζ (2 ≤ i ≤ d). (iv) There is an injective multiplicative map c : H −→ K whose image is disjoint from {1K, Ω}. We write ch = c(h); this map is not required to preserve identities or zeros. (v) There is an element z ∈ H such that the map (τ, τ′ ) 7−→ κ(τ)zκ(τ′ ) is an injection from (T \ {0T })2 into H \ {ζ}.
